clue.text: Opportunist in luck by river

parts.note: to be in luck is to have a lucky chance
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A lucky opportunist sits down beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is someone who grabs every opening for personal gain, an informal word for an opportunist.

clue.text: Sword wound girl shows

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl displays the wound a sword gave her.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short, curved, broad-bladed sword once used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Imposing, old Pinochet?

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A description of the former Chilean dictator as an imposing old man.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Pinochet is an example: the answer is his first name, Augusto Pinochet having ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto was the forename of the Chilean general Pinochet, so the surname stands for his given name by example.

clue.text: A fitness regime doing the rounds?

definitions.text: A fitness regime doing the rounds?

parts.words: A fitness regime doing the rounds?
parts.note: surface reading: an exercise fad that is currently popular and going round
setter's reading: a workout where you move round a series of exercise stations in a loop

explanation.surface: A trendy exercise programme everyone seems to be talking about.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of exercise has people move through a sequence of stations in a repeated loop, literally going round.

clue.text: I turn aria, with new arrangement, into Land of Hope …

indicators.note: giving words a new arrangement means putting their letters in a different order

explanation.surface: A singer reworks an aria into Land of Hope and Glory.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots suggest Land of Hope and Glory, but Hope here is the novelist Anthony Hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary central European kingdom invented by Anthony Hope in The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Does, raving about extremely good dual-purpose item of furniture

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
raving suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means extremely good

explanation.surface: Female deer go wild over a fabulous piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Does reads as a verb but is the plural of doe, used only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa bed serves as a sofa by day and unfolds into a bed at night, so it has two uses.

clue.text: In the morning US soldiers brought over a Greek character

indicators.note: brought over suggests being flipped across, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: American troops escort a Greek person over one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of S.

clue.text: A novel that may give one enjoyment on a liner at sea — capital!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A book makes good reading for a passenger on an ocean cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after: the enjoyment comes first, then the shuffled liner, then the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Funeral in Berlin is a 1964 spy novel by Len Deighton, later filmed with Michael Caine.

clue.text: Cake — bishop, note, about to have one

indicators.note: about means going round, so the note wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cleric is invited to tea and about to be given cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small, dense chocolate cake cut into squares.

clue.text: In in 24 hours, coming from Benin some time ago

indicators.note: the second in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone stays indoors all day after arriving from West Africa long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled In in looks like a typo; the first one is a word meaning at home, the second places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was the name of the West African country until 1975, when it was renamed Benin.

clue.text: Row about grand Asian animal

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row goes round the other letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a big Asian beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a big cat native to Asia, from India to Siberia.

clue.text: Jo, in loose sarong, having hot Indian dish

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the other letters
loose means not held in order, so the letters are freed to rearrange

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A woman named Jo, wearing a loose sarong, orders a hot curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogan josh is an aromatic lamb curry from Kashmiri cuisine.

clue.text: A sailor reportedly delivered from storm

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by someone, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is rescued from a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Storm looks like weather, but it is the verb for attacking a fortified place.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to assault it, a sudden violent attack.

clue.text: American ringing friend in UNICEF, perhaps

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: An American phones a friend who works at UNICEF.
explanation.definitionFit: UNICEF is formed from the initial letters of United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund, so it is one example of such a word.

clue.text: Filming group of spectators where there's target practice

parts.note: shooting a film is filming it
a gallery is a group of onlookers, as at a golf tournament

explanation.surface: A film crew and onlookers gather at a firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting gallery is a range, often at a fairground, where people fire at targets.

clue.text: Objective absorbing Italian, one to act independently

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the first word holds the next piece inside it

explanation.surface: An Italian's aim is to act on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for doing something without help from anyone else.

clue.text: Remark by picket in lookout

parts.note: a picket is a pointed stake or post

explanation.surface: A comment made by a striker on a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: Picket suggests a striker, but it is a fence stake.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a position from which soldiers watch the enemy, a lookout.

clue.text: Backhanded slash

definitions.meaning: first meaning: indirect, as in a backhanded compliment
second meaning: the forward-slanting stroke used in typing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a tennis or swordplay stroke; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an indirect remark, and as a noun names the slanting punctuation stroke.

clue.text: Worker employed in excellent US city

indicators.note: employed in means working within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: safe is British slang for excellent or cool
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An employee lands a great job in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Safe as slang for excellent or great is British youth usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of the US state of New Mexico.

clue.text: Threatening disaster? Nothing less, without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes round the element

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A warning that catastrophe is near, unless the air supply runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Without normally means lacking; here it means outside, so the oxygen goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ominous gives a sense that misfortune is coming, so it threatens disaster.

clue.text: Missile — fuss about right drill

indicators.note: about means going round, so the fuss surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise drill at school

explanation.surface: A fuss is made over a correct missile drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile fired from ships and submarines.

clue.text: Freckle on leg — it's misshapen

indicators.note: misshapen means badly formed, so the letters are put into another form

explanation.surface: Someone points out a freckle on a leg that has an odd shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is the medical term for a small pigmented spot on the skin, like a freckle.

clue.text: Egg-shaped object, initially empty

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word before it

explanation.surface: An egg-shaped thing that turns out to be hollow at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg-shaped object looks like one phrase, but only Egg-shaped is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from the Latin for egg and describes something with an oval, egg-like form.

clue.text: Terribly irate about the Spanish studio

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the article
terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a Spanish artist's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, a French word for studio.

clue.text: Low Sunday bellringer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Sunday after Easter
second meaning: the hunchback bellringer of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel

explanation.walkthrough: Low Sunday, the first Sunday after Easter, is also called Quasimodo Sunday from the opening words of its Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the church feast after Easter and to the famous bellringer in Hugo's novel.

clue.text: Free, toilets on Euston, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start, the very first letter of the station name

explanation.surface: Free use of the toilets at Euston station in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British for toilet; Euston is a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free, as an animal that has broken its tether and is unrestrained.

clue.text: Came out of Egypt's capital, then joined forces

indicators.note: capital here means the capital letter, the one at the head of the word

parts.note: to merge is to join forces

explanation.surface: A people leave Egypt's capital and unite.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like Cairo, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, so emerged is the past tense of coming out.

clue.text: Don Pasquale's nephew, tense or relaxed?

indicators.note: relaxed suggests loosened, so the letters are free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a character in an opera is uptight or calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Pasquale is a comic opera by Donizetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernesto is the young nephew whom the old bachelor tries to disinherit in Donizetti's opera Don Pasquale.
